content.title: About
content.content: Hot chocolate made with low‑fat (1 %) or fat‑free (skim) milk is a beverage combining cocoa powder, sugar, and milk with very little fat. It retains a rich chocolate flavor while providing fewer calories and saturated fats than traditional hot chocolate made with whole milk.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cocoa powder is rich in flavonoids, which have antioxidant properties.
Skim milk retains most of the protein and calcium but virtually no fat.
Hot chocolate originated in Mexico, where cacao was consumed by ancient civilizations.
In the United States hot chocolate is often topped with whipped cream, which is omitted in low‑fat versions.
Cocoa can be natural or Dutch‑processed, affecting color and acidity of the drink.

items.title: Rich in flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids from cocoa support vascular function and reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Skim milk provides a high level of calcium essential for bone health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The drink typically contains less than 1 % fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium aids normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Cocoa stimulates serotonin and endorphin production, helping improve mood.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or lactose may react even to skim milk.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Hot chocolate often contains added sugar, which can raise the beverage’s glycemic index.

items.title: Caffeine and theobromine
items.content: Cocoa contains small amounts of caffeine and theobromine, which may affect sleep if consumed in large quantities.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Cocoa contains oxalates that, in excess, may contribute to kidney stone formation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the milk, add cocoa powder and sugar to taste, and whisk until smooth. Optional: stir in a pinch of vanilla or cinnamon for extra aroma. Serve hot, optionally topped with a dollop of whipped low‑fat cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cocoa powder in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Keep skim milk refrigerated and use within 5–7 days after opening.
